clue.text: Laser beam on stage

parts.note: a playful description of the strong lamp that picks out a performer in a theatre, made to sound like science fiction

explanation.surface: A dazzling laser effect is shone across a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre lamp throwing a concentrated circle of light on one performer is the thing described.

clue.text: See slip perhaps through the coat

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone notices an undergarment showing through an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of SEE SLIP; 'through the' only links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or fur-trimmed jacket, a kind of outer garment.

clue.text: Sort of overture to many a jazz fan included

indicators.note: included means one piece is placed inside the run of the others

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz lover is treated to some kind of musical opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts CAT inside TO, C and A, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, often used as an opening or prelude.

clue.text: A suit Len designed to keep the heat in

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are fashioned into a new pattern, an anagram

explanation.surface: A tailor named Len makes a warm suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the letters of A SUIT LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To insulate is to wrap something so warmth does not escape.

clue.text: Irritable etc, in your old surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the old word for your goes round the other piece

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Someone grows cross about all the et ceteras around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' places ETC inside THY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy is a synonym for bad-tempered or crotchety.

clue.text: Boring i.e.a wayward native inhabitant

indicators.note: wayward letters stray from their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull and wilful local person is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges the letters of BORING, IE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original indigenous dweller of a land.

clue.text: He had a ready-made home quite naturally

definitions.text: He had a ready-made home quite naturally

parts.words: He had a ready-made home quite naturally
parts.note: a prehistoric person moved into a home that nature had already hollowed out of rock

explanation.surface: Someone moved into a home that needed no building.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone Age people sheltered in rock caves provided by nature rather than built.

clue.text: Simon's to overact in a heavy overcoat

parts.note: the apostle Simon was called Peter, so Simon's gives Peter plus S
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: Someone named Simon plays a theatrical part in a bulky coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham is a heavy greatcoat named after a Regency viscount.

clue.text: Include a demonstration of affection

definitions.meaning: to take in or comprise, as a scheme takes in ideas

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to comprise and a hug showing fondness.

clue.text: Sugar to stick round lettuce

indicators.note: round means the word for sticking surrounds the salad leaf

parts.note: to glue is to stick
cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Sweetener is used to fix something round a salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar found in fruit and blood.

clue.text: Late train?

parts.note: late can mean deceased, and a train a procession, so a procession for the dead

explanation.surface: A delayed railway service is grumbled about.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession following the deceased.

clue.text: His belt's a problem to fix

indicators.note: a problem with the letters means they are disordered, an anagram

explanation.surface: A man's belt has gone wrong and needs repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges the letters of HIS BELTS A.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish is to set up or settle something firmly.

clue.text: Main road?

parts.note: main is an old word for the open sea, so a road across the main is a shipping route

explanation.surface: A principal highway is asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lane is a regular route followed by ships across the ocean.

clue.text: It is singularly held to improve one's vision

definitions.text: It is singularly held to improve one's vision

parts.words: It is singularly held to improve one's vision
parts.note: singularly means one lens only, held in the eye, as opposed to spectacles

explanation.surface: Something is held in a special way to help someone see.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens held in one eye socket to correct sight.

clue.text: Old teacher panted terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled, an anagram

explanation.surface: A former schoolmaster gasped for breath badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedant formerly meant a schoolmaster before it meant a fussy stickler.

clue.text: See following summary-just

indicators.note: following means the bishop's seat comes after the summary

parts.note: a precis is a summary
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

explanation.surface: Look at the notes that come next, a summary and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely and just both mean exactly, as in 'just so'.

clue.text: Hurried up with despicable person taking one on account

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ran means hurried
a rat is a contemptible person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A villain rushed off with someone's money from their account.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken or written account of events.

clue.text: With hidden energy, Ali on a restored harp

indicators.note: with something hidden means one letter is tucked inside the rest
restored means the letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Ali vigorously repairs an old harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges ALI ON A, and 'With hidden' tucks E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aeolian harp is a wind-played instrument, so the adjective stands for it.

clue.text: Checked retreads that had been repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters are reassembled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Tyres with new treads were inspected after being mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted or stopped, as progress is checked.

clue.text: Father puts cloth on the model

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Dad drapes fabric over a mannequin.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to be imitated.

clue.text: Improvement for most of the military mechanics going round

indicators.note: going round means the shortened corps surrounds the next word
most of means the final letter of the corps's abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, the British Army's repair corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers walk round making things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims REME to REM; 'going round' puts FOR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change for the better.

clue.text: Over-fastidious person to worry over top spin

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the worrying word sits above the next piece

parts.note: to fuss is to worry

indicators.note: spin turns the word round so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A fussy person frets about spinning a top.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone who makes too much of trivial details.

clue.text: Excellent specimen of a snake

definitions.meaning: informal term for a first-rate example of something
a short name for a rattlesnake

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: dated slang for a cracking example, and a rattlesnake for short.

clue.text: One who has no standing at the meeting?

definitions.text: One who has no standing at the meeting?

parts.words: One who has no standing at the meeting?
parts.note: the person presiding is seated, so literally never standing, rather than lacking status

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting is said to have no authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The presiding officer of a meeting sits in the chair, so is never standing.

clue.text: Type of plant book

definitions.meaning: a plant living one season only
a yearbook, such as a children's yearly gift volume

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a plant completing its life in one year and a yearly publication.

clue.text: Need not a luxury

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe something essential that cannot be done without.

clue.text: Old Greek has a duty in hospital

indicators.note: in means the duty is placed inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
a part is one's share of duty, as in doing one's part

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek works a shift on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: A dotty way to produce a picture

definitions.text: A dotty way to produce a picture

parts.words: A dotty way to produce a picture
parts.note: dotty here means made of dots rather than crazy

explanation.surface: Someone paints in a crazy fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipple is the technique of building up shading with many small dots.

clue.text: Girl from Orleans endlessly has ring included

indicators.note: included means the round letter is put inside the rest
from signals the letters are made into something new, an anagram
endlessly means the last letter of the town name is dropped

parts.note: the French city
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A young woman from Orléans wears a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ORLEANS to ORLEAN, 'from' rearranges it, and 'included' places O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonora is a female first name, as in Beethoven's heroine.

clue.text: Praiseworthy double turn by a politician

indicators.note: turn means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: dual means double
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician does a double act on stage and wins praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means expressing praise, glossed loosely as deserving it.
